title: Genomewide DNA methylation analysis in combat veterans reveals a novel locus for PTSD
authors: Mehta D., Bruenig D., Carrillo‐Roa T., Lawford B., Harvey W., Morris C. P., Smith A. K., Binder E. B., Young R. McD, Voisey J.
design: Human blood methylation and expression; 96 veterans and 115 independent replication participants
summary: Lower methylation at DOCK2 cg16277944 was associated with greater PTSD symptom severity and replicated in a separate cohort (p = 0.0028). Post-hoc blood analyses found a modest inverse methylation–expression association (r = −0.21) and a group difference in DOCK2 expression.
limitation: Cross-sectional, male samples; discovery used a 10% false-discovery-rate threshold. Association does not establish intervention responsiveness. Genetic variation also influenced methylation. The 211 participants are the total across both cohorts, not the discovery sample alone.
sourceAccess: Relevant full-text methods and results reviewed

summary: DOCK2 appeared among nominally associated loci shared between sperm and blood. This extends the tissue question raised by the earlier veteran study.

title: Using Monozygotic Twins to Dissect Common Genes in Posttraumatic Stress Disorder and Migraine
authors: Bainomugisa C et al.
design: Blood methylation; six identical-twin pairs discordant for PTSD
summary: DOCK2 was among candidate genes with methylation associations surviving gene-wise Bonferroni correction. The design matches inherited sequence and many demographic factors within twin pairs. Separate migraine analyses also implicated DOCK2.
limitation: Only 12 PTSD-study participants. This is support at the gene level, without confirmed replication here of cg16277944. Different CpG sites changed in different directions. Gene-wise correction is distinct from genome-wide discovery significance, and migraine overlap limits specificity.
sourceAccess: Relevant full-text methods and results reviewed
